at eksplodere.explanation: "At eksplodere" means "to explode". To say someone loses control of their feelings, use it for anger: "Han eksploderede af vrede" (He exploded with anger).

at eksportere.explanation: "At eksportere" means "to export". To say you send a file out of a program, use it with the file: "at eksportere en fil" (to export a file).

at elske.explanation: "At elske" means "to love". To tell a person you love them, say: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you). To say you love a food, use the same verb: "Jeg elsker pizza" (I love pizza).

at ende.explanation: "At ende" means "to end". To say a story or event finishes a certain way, say: "Historien endte godt" (The story ended well). To say where you finally arrive, it also means "to end up": "Vi endte i Aarhus" (We ended up in Aarhus).

at ende med.explanation: "At ende med" means "to end up with". To name what you are left with, put a noun after it: "Jeg endte med en forkølelse" (I ended up with a cold). To say what you finally did, add "at" (to) and a verb: "Han endte med at købe en cykel" (He ended up buying a bike).

at enes.explanation: "At enes" means "to agree / get along". To say what people agree on, use "om" (about) after it: "Vi enedes om prisen" (We agreed on the price). To say people do not get along, add "ikke" (not): "De kan ikke enes" (They cannot get along).

at engagere sig.explanation: "At engagere sig" means "to get involved". To name what you get involved in, put "i" (in) before it: "Hun engagerer sig i den lokale idrætsklub" (She gets involved in the local sports club).

at erfare.explanation: "At erfare" means "to find out / experience". To name the fact you learned, add "at" (that) and a full sentence: "Jeg har erfaret, at toget er forsinket" (I have found out that the train is late).

at erklære.explanation: "At erklære" means "to declare". To say a country starts a war, say: "Landet erklærer krig" (The country declares war). To say you tell someone how you feel, use it with the feeling: "at erklære sin kærlighed" (to declare your love).

at erobre.explanation: "At erobre" means "to conquer". To say a company wins over customers, use it with the market: "at erobre markedet" (to conquer the market).

at erstatte.explanation: "At erstatte" means "to replace". To say you pay someone back for a loss, use it with the damage: "at erstatte en skade" (to compensate for damage).

at etablere.explanation: "At etablere" means "to establish". To say you set up your own place in a job or town, add "sig" (oneself): "Hun har etableret sig som tandlæge" (She has set herself up as a dentist).

at evakuere.explanation: "At evakuere" means "to evacuate". To name the place that is emptied, put it right after the verb: "at evakuere skolen" (to evacuate the school).

at evaluere.explanation: "At evaluere" means "to evaluate". To name what you judge, put it right after the verb: "Vi skal evaluere kurset" (We must evaluate the course).

e-boks.explanation: "En e-Boks" means "an e-Boks". It is the digital mailbox in Denmark where public offices, banks and companies send you letters. To tell someone to look for a letter, say: "Tjek din e-Boks" (Check your e-Boks).

eddike.explanation: "Eddike" means "vinegar". To say how much you add to a dish, use it with an amount: "en teskefuld eddike" (a teaspoon of vinegar).

effektiv.explanation: "Effektiv" means "efficient". When a remedy or tool works well, it also means "effective": "et effektivt middel" (an effective remedy).

efter.explanation: "Efter" means "after". When you search for something, it means "for": "at lede efter nøglerne" (to look for the keys). To put a whole sentence after "after", add "at" (that): "efter at jeg kom hjem" (after I came home).

efter min mening.explanation: "Efter min mening" means "in my opinion". It is built from "efter" (according to), "min" (my) and "en mening" (an opinion).

efterfølgende.explanation: "Efterfølgende" means "afterwards". It is built from "efter" (after) and "at følge" (to follow). When you name a day that comes next, put it before the noun, where it means "following": "den efterfølgende dag" (the following day).

efterhånden.explanation: "Efterhånden" means "gradually". When you say a feeling has built up over time, it means "by now": "Jeg er efterhånden træt af det" (I am getting tired of it by now).

efterhånden som.explanation: "Efterhånden som" means "as". To say one thing changes step by step while another goes on, use it before the clause: "Jeg bliver bedre, efterhånden som jeg øver" (I get better as I practice). To say two things only happen at the same time, use "mens" (while) instead: "Mens jeg øver, drikker jeg te" (While I practice, I drink tea).

efterlyst.explanation: "Efterlyst" means "wanted", as in a person the police are searching for. It comes from the verb "at efterlyse" (to put out a call for): "Politiet efterlyser vidner" (The police are asking for witnesses).

eftersom.explanation: "Eftersom" means "since", as in giving a reason. It is built from "efter" (after) and "som" (as).

efterspørgsel.explanation: "En efterspørgsel" means "a demand". To name what people want, add "på" after it: "efterspørgsel på billige boliger" (demand for cheap homes).

eftersøgt.explanation: "Eftersøgt" means "wanted", as in a person or thing that people are looking for. It comes from the verb "at eftersøge" (to search for): "Politiet eftersøger tyven" (The police are searching for the thief). When many people want to hire someone, it also means "in demand": "en eftersøgt ekspert" (an expert in demand).

eftertragtet.explanation: "Eftertragtet" means "sought-after". It comes from the verb "at tragte efter" (to strive for): "Han tragter efter magt" (He strives for power).

egen.explanation: "Egen" means "own". To say you did something without help, use the phrase "på egen hånd" (by yourself): "Jeg gjorde det på egen hånd" (I did it by myself).

egentlig.explanation: "Egentlig" means "actually". To say the plan was different from what happened, say: "Jeg skulle egentlig arbejde, men jeg er syg" (I was supposed to be working, but I am sick). To ask something you have been wondering about, put it at the end: "Hvad hedder du egentlig?" (What is your name, actually?)

egnet.explanation: "Egnet" means "suitable". To name the person or purpose, add "til" (for): "Filmen er egnet til børn" (The film is suitable for children).

egoistisk.explanation: "Egoistisk" means "selfish". To say the opposite, use "uselvisk" (unselfish): "en uselvisk hjælper" (an unselfish helper).

ejendele.explanation: "Ejendele" means "belongings". To tell someone to bring their things, say: "Tag dine ejendele med" (Take your belongings with you). Do not mix it up with "en ejendom" (a property): "Ejendommen er til salg" (The property is for sale).

ejendommelig.explanation: "Ejendommelig" means "peculiar". When you say a feature belongs to a place, add "for" (for): "Dialekten er ejendommelig for egnen" (The dialect is characteristic of the area). Here it means "characteristic".

eksisterende.explanation: "Eksisterende" means "existing". It comes from the verb "at eksistere" (to exist). To set it against "ny" (new), say: "nye og eksisterende kunder" (new and existing customers).

eksklusiv.explanation: "Eksklusiv" means "exclusive". When you give a price without tax, it means "excluding": "100 kr. eksklusiv moms" (100 kr. excluding VAT). "Moms" (VAT) is the Danish sales tax.

eksport.explanation: "En eksport" means "an export". To name the goods you export, add "af" (of): "eksport af maskiner" (export of machines).

ekstra.explanation: "Ekstra" means "extra". To make a word stronger, put "ekstra" before it: "ekstra god" (extra good).

ekstraordinær.explanation: "Ekstraordinær" means "extraordinary". To praise something far better than normal, say: "en ekstraordinær præstation" (an extraordinary achievement). To say something is outside the normal schedule, say: "et ekstraordinært møde" (an extraordinary meeting).

ekstrem.explanation: "Ekstrem" means "extreme". To say "extremely", use the form "ekstremt": "Det er ekstremt koldt" (It is extremely cold).

ekstremt.explanation: "Ekstremt" means "extremely". To say something is more than "meget" (very), put it before the word: "Det var ekstremt svært" (It was extremely hard).

elegant.explanation: "Elegant" means "elegant". To say someone moves gracefully, add it to the verb: "Hun danser meget elegant" (She dances very elegantly). To praise a clever answer, say: "en elegant løsning" (an elegant solution).

elektricitet.explanation: "Elektricitet" means "electricity". To say the power is out, use "strøm" (power): "Strømmen er gået" (The power is out).

elektrisk.explanation: "Elektrisk" means "electric". To say there is no power, use "strøm" (power): "Der er ingen strøm" (There is no power).

elektronik.explanation: "Elektronik" means "electronics". It is used without an article: "Jeg sparer op til ny elektronik" (I am saving up for new electronics).

elendig.explanation: "Elendig" means "terrible". To say you feel terrible, say: "Jeg har det elendigt" (I feel terrible). To say a person is very bad at something, say: "Han er en elendig sanger" (He is a terrible singer).

eller.explanation: "Eller" means "or". To check that someone agrees, add it at the end of a question: "Du kommer, eller?" (You are coming, right?). Do not mix it up with "ellers" (otherwise): "Skynd dig, ellers kommer vi for sent" (Hurry up, or we will be late).

ellers.explanation: "Ellers" means "or else". When you ask for more, it means "else": "Hvem ellers?" (Who else?). Do not mix it up with "eller" (or), which joins two choices: "te eller kaffe" (tea or coffee).

elleve.explanation: "Elleve" means "eleven". To say "eleventh", use "elvte": "den elvte maj" (May eleventh).

elvte.explanation: "Elvte" means "eleventh". It comes from the number "elleve" (eleven). To use the other spelling, write "ellevte": "den ellevte maj" (May eleventh).

empati.explanation: "Empati" means "empathy". Do not mix it up with "medlidenhed" (pity), which is feeling sorry for someone: "Jeg har medlidenhed med hende" (I feel pity for her).

en e-mail.explanation: "En e-mail" means "an email". To say it the short way, drop the "e-": "Jeg sender dig en mail" (I will send you an email).

en edderkop.explanation: "En edderkop" means "a spider". To say you fear spiders, use the plural: "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am afraid of spiders).

en effekt.explanation: "En effekt" means "an effect". To say something does not work, say: "Det har ingen effekt" (It has no effect).

en efterforsker.explanation: "En efterforsker" means "an investigator". It comes from the verb "at efterforske" (to investigate): "Politiet efterforsker sagen" (The police are investigating the case).

en efterforskning.explanation: "En efterforskning" means "an investigation". It comes from the verb "at efterforske" (to investigate). To say it has begun, say: "Politiet har indledt en efterforskning" (The police have started an investigation).

en efterfølger.explanation: "En efterfølger" means "a successor". To say a film has a follow-up, use it for a sequel: "Filmen fik en efterfølger" (The film got a sequel).

en efterløn.explanation: "En efterløn" means "an early-retirement pension". It is a Danish scheme that people can pay into through an unemployment fund. It is built from "efter" (after) and "en løn" (a wage).

en eftermiddag.explanation: "En eftermiddag" means "an afternoon". To say something happens in the afternoon, use "om eftermiddagen" (in the afternoon): "Jeg træner om eftermiddagen" (I work out in the afternoon). To say "this afternoon", use "i eftermiddag": "Vi ses i eftermiddag" (See you this afternoon).

en eftermiddagskaffe.explanation: "En eftermiddagskaffe" means "an afternoon coffee". It is built from "eftermiddag" (afternoon) and "en kaffe" (a coffee). To invite someone over, say: "Kom forbi til eftermiddagskaffe" (Come by for afternoon coffee).

en efterskole.explanation: "En efterskole" means "a boarding school". It is a Danish school for students aged 14 to 18 that they choose to attend instead of the last years at a regular school. To say you go to one, use "på" (at): "Hun går på efterskole" (She goes to boarding school).

en efterårsdag.explanation: "En efterårsdag" means "a fall day". It is built from "efterår" (fall) and "en dag" (a day). To say something happens in the fall, use "i efteråret" (in the fall): "Bladene falder af træerne i efteråret" (The leaves fall from the trees in the fall).

en efterårsferie.explanation: "En efterårsferie" means "a fall break". In Denmark, schools have it as a week off in October. It is built from "efterår" (fall) and "ferie" (vacation).

en eg.explanation: "En eg" means "an oak". The "the" form "egen" is spelled like the word "egen" (own). To say "the oak", use it as a noun: "Egen står i haven" (The oak stands in the garden). To say "own", use it before a noun: "min egen bil" (my own car).

en egenskab.explanation: "En egenskab" means "a quality". It is built from "egen" (own) and the ending "-skab", as in "venskab" (friendship). To name a good quality, say: "en god egenskab" (a good quality).

en ejendom.explanation: "En ejendom" means "a property", as in a building with its land. To mark a place as owned by a private person, say: "Privat ejendom" (Private property).

en ejendomsmægler.explanation: "En ejendomsmægler" means "a real estate agent". The part "ejendom" means "property". The part "mægler" means "broker", as in "en børsmægler" (a stockbroker).

en ejer.explanation: "En ejer" means "an owner". It comes from "at eje" (to own). To name what someone owns, add "af" (of): "ejeren af huset" (the owner of the house).

en ejerbolig.explanation: "En ejerbolig" means "an owner-occupied home". It is built from "ejer" (owner) and "en bolig" (a home).

en ejerlejlighed.explanation: "En ejerlejlighed" means "a condominium". It is built from "ejer" (owner) and "en lejlighed" (an apartment).

en eks.explanation: "En eks" means "an ex". To say it in full, use "en ekskæreste" (an ex-boyfriend / ex-girlfriend): "Min ekskæreste bor i Odense" (My ex lives in Odense).

en eksamen.explanation: "En eksamen" means "an exam". To say you sit one, use "at tage eksamen" (to take an exam): "Hun tager eksamen i juni" (She takes her exam in June).

en eksaminator.explanation: "En eksaminator" means "an examiner". In a Danish oral exam, it is the teacher who asks the questions. Do not mix it up with "en censor" (an external examiner), who helps set the grade: "Censoren giver karakteren sammen med læreren" (The external examiner gives the grade together with the teacher).

en eksistens.explanation: "En eksistens" means "an existence". To call someone a shady person, use it for a person: "en tvivlsom eksistens" (a shady character).

en ekskursion.explanation: "En ekskursion" means "a field trip". Do not mix it up with "en udflugt" (a day out for fun): "Vi tog på udflugt til stranden" (We went on an outing to the beach).

en ekskæreste.explanation: "En ekskæreste" means "an ex". It is built from "eks" (former) and "en kæreste" (a boyfriend or girlfriend). The word "kæreste" is the same for men and women: "Hun er min kæreste" (She is my girlfriend).

en eksmand.explanation: "En eksmand" means "an ex-husband". It is built from "eks" (former) and "en mand" (a man or husband). To say "my husband", use "min mand": "Min mand er hjemme" (My husband is home).

en ekspedient.explanation: "En ekspedient" means "a store clerk". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Hun er ekspedient" (She is a store clerk).

en ekspedition.explanation: "En ekspedition" means "a service / transaction". When you mean a long trip to explore a place, it means "an expedition": "en ekspedition til Grønland" (an expedition to Greenland).

related.en: to handle a person at a counter

en ekspert.explanation: "En ekspert" means "an expert". To name the subject, add "i" (in): "Hun er ekspert i vin" (She is an expert in wine).

en eksplosion.explanation: "En eksplosion" means "an explosion". To say prices jump suddenly, say: "en eksplosion i priserne" (a sudden jump in prices).

en elastik.explanation: "En elastik" means "a rubber band". To say clothes have a stretchy band in them, it means "elastic": "Der er elastik i bukserne" (There is elastic in the pants).

en elbil.explanation: "En elbil" means "an electric car". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en bil" (a car). The same "el" starts "en elcykel" (an electric bike).

en elefant.explanation: "En elefant" means "an elephant". To say someone is clumsy, use the saying "som en elefant i en porcelænsbutik" (like an elephant in a china shop).

en elektriker.explanation: "En elektriker" means "an electrician". To say what someone does for a living, leave out "en": "Min bror er elektriker" (My brother is an electrician).

en elektronikbutik.explanation: "En elektronikbutik" means "an electronics store". It is built from "elektronik" (electronics) and "en butik" (a store).

en elev.explanation: "En elev" means "a pupil". When you talk about someone learning a trade at a workplace, it means "a trainee": "Hun er elev hos en elektriker" (She is a trainee with an electrician). For university, use "en studerende" (a student): "Han er studerende" (He is a student).

en elevator.explanation: "En elevator" means "an elevator". The word "en lift" (a lift) means the same: "Liften er i stykker" (The lift is broken). To say you travel by it, use "med" (by): "Vi kører med elevatoren" (We go by the elevator).

en elg.explanation: "En elg" means "a moose / elk". Do not mix it up with "et rensdyr" (a reindeer): "Rensdyret lever i Lapland" (The reindeer lives in Lapland).

en elkedel.explanation: "En elkedel" means "an electric kettle". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en kedel" (a kettle). The same "el" starts "en elbil" (an electric car).

en elpære.explanation: "En elpære" means "a light bulb". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en pære" (a pear), because the bulb is shaped like one. The same "pære" is the fruit: "Jeg spiser en pære" (I eat a pear).

en elregning.explanation: "En elregning" means "an electricity bill". It is built from "el" (electricity) and "en regning" (a bill). The same "regning" is in the phrase for asking for the check: "Regningen, tak" (The check, please).

en elskerinde.explanation: "En elskerinde" means "a mistress". It comes from "at elske" (to love). The ending "-inde" marks a woman, as in "en sangerinde" (a female singer).

en embedsmand.explanation: "En embedsmand" means "a civil servant". It is built from "et embede" (a public post) and "en mand" (a man).

en emhætte.explanation: "En emhætte" means "a range hood". To tell someone to switch it on, say: "Tænd for emhætten" (Turn on the range hood).

en emission.explanation: "En emission" means "an emission". In finance it has another meaning, a company selling new shares: "en emission af aktier" (an issue of shares).

en emoji.explanation: "En emoji" means "an emoji". To say you sent one in a message, say: "Jeg sendte en glad emoji" (I sent a happy emoji).

en encyklopædi.explanation: "En encyklopædi" means "an encyclopedia". Spell it with "k" and "æ", not "c" and "ae". The word "et leksikon" (an encyclopedia) means the same: "Jeg slog det op i et leksikon" (I looked it up in an encyclopedia).

en ende.explanation: "En ende" means "an end". To say where something lies, use "i enden af" (at the end of): "Huset ligger i enden af korridoren" (The house lies at the end of the hallway). For the end of a story, use "en slutning" (an ending) instead: "Filmen har en god slutning" (The film has a good ending).

en endelse.explanation: "En endelse" means "an ending (of a word)". To see one, take "talede" (spoke): the ending is "-ede". For the end of a story, use "en slutning" (a conclusion): "Bogen har en trist slutning" (The book has a sad ending).

en endestation.explanation: "En endestation" means "a terminus / last stop". It is built from "ende" (end) and "en station" (a station). The part "ende" is also in "i enden af gaden" (at the end of the street).
